changes: Added a read-only, advisory Experience Layer referential re-validation instrument: (1) an optional bounded anchorFiles[] on the derived FindingSignal (with :line[:col] suffix stripped to bare repo paths), (2) a pure leaf core/experience-revalidation.ts (revalidateSignals + computeValidRate, anchored-only denominator, never NaN), and (3) a read-only learning_validate CLI that derives finding-signals through the store ports (no persist) and reports valid-rate / drift-rate of accumulated signals against the current git HEAD. Registered consistently across cli-engine, registry, config DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS, command-policy (readOnly/all/none), READ_ONLY_COMMANDS, and process-fact-levels. No gate, no finding-lifecycle write, no scoring change, nothing persisted.
usage: Run `node bin/lattice.js learning_validate` for the human report; `learning_validate '{"json":true}'` for the machine-readable ValidRateReport; `learning_validate '{"story":"<id>"}'` to restrict to one story.
expectedOutcome: A terminal report showing signals total/anchored/valid/stale/unanchored plus valid-rate and drift-rate and a list of stale signals, marked advisory/read-only.
actualTranscript: learning_validate prints valid-rate 0.926 / drift-rate 0.074 at HEAD (25 valid, 2 stale, 4 unanchored of 31 signals); --json emits a well-formed object with all numeric fields + staleSignals[]; --story B-7561 restricts to 2 signals (validRate 1.0); --story B-zzzz (nonexistent) yields all-zero with no crash; git status is unchanged before/after (read-only confirmed).
outcomeDiff: Matches expected. The 0.926/0.074 signal-level numbers are consistent with Baseline A's finding-level 0.92/0.08, cross-validating the instrument.
limitations: Existence-based exact-path matching: a directory-style anchor (e.g. packages/main/src) is conservatively reported stale because git ls-tree -r lists only blobs — this over-reports rather than hides drift (the safe direction for a staleness detector). The stronger blob-equality 'unchanged since the finding was confirmed' tier is deferred to a later forward-capture story (it needs the confirmation HEAD recorded per finding). The metric is signal-level (the unit the Experience Layer surfaces), not finding-level.
pitfalls: This is an advisory instrument only: it never changes gates, scoring, promptHash, or the surfaced signals, and persists nothing. valid-rate is signal-level, so it is a different (though consistent) unit from Baseline A's finding-level drift number; do not compare them as if identical. It does not by itself prove the Experience Layer makes development smarter — that forward A/B proof is a separate later step.
